svg.title: Three Days, Two Nights
svg.desc: A one-minute comic in 7 panels. Three columns side by side: The Preparation, The Sabbath and The first day, row for row. Panel 1 (Mark 14:17-72): evening indoors by lamplight, Jesus seated with His disciples. Caption: "The Passover meal, the arrest, the trials." Counted: Alive. Panel 2 (Mark 15:46): the tomb at night, its stone rolled across the entrance. Caption: "In the tomb, the stone rolled against it." Counted: Night 1. Panel 3 (Mark 16:1): three women in a street at night, each carrying a jar of spices. Caption: "“When the Sabbath was past,” the women buy spices." Counted: Night 2. Panel 4 (Mark 15:33-46): three crosses on a rise under a darkened sky. Caption: "“The day before the Sabbath”: crucified, buried before evening." Counted: Day 1 · part. Panel 5 (Luke 23:56): the women seated at rest indoors, their jars beside them. Caption: "“On the Sabbath they rested according to the commandment.”" Counted: Day 2 · all. Panel 6 (Mark 16:2; Luke 24:13-21): two disciples walk the road to Emmaus with Jesus, whom they do not recognise. Caption: "Sunrise: the tomb is empty. Later, on the road to Emmaus:". Cleopas says: "It is now the third day since these things happened." Counted: Day 3 · part. Panel 7 (Matthew 12:40). Caption: "Three days touched. Two nights. The third night is the cost the Friday reading carries." The count: alive, Day 1 part, Night 1, Day 2 all, Night 2, Day 3 part, Night 3. "Three days touched. Two nights. The third night is the cost the Friday reading carries." The point: Mark names the day He died, “the day before the Sabbath,” and Luke counts that Sunday “the third day.” The Friday reading keeps both, and owes one night.
svg.text: The week as the Hebrew calendar counts it, sunset to sunset
Mark names the day He died, “the day before the
Sabbath,” and Luke counts that Sunday “the third day.”
The Friday reading keeps both, and owes one night.
Each Hebrew day begins at sunset, so its night comes first. Weekdays follow this study's Friday reading.
